tweets.text:
$ETH The move indeed wasn't done yet as per the initial tweet.

It can be very enticing to buy the blood after the initial candle, but when price keeps grinding down and there has been no proper flush, very rarely does it turn around. Usually it is just anticipation before the big one. Which is exactly what we saw and why I highlighted that it wasn't the dip to buy yet.

But the big change since then is that on yesterday's big candle you finally saw the Open Interest flush with a lot of long liquidations. That is the sign you want to see for local reversals, which is what we've already been seeing now.

Now things have reset, funding is roughly flat and price has slowly retraced that last candle without open interest going back in.

So most fuel on both sides is out now. It will be up to the spot flows from here.

Mark out your high timeframe levels and play it level by level.

tweets.text:
I’m starting to see AI agents do financial research more like a real desk.

Pull context from across the web, then check it against prices, history, and session-level moves.

That second step is still the weak point. Most agents reconstruct market facts from articles and commentary, which breaks down when precision matters.

The split is simple. One system finds what happened and why. Another provides the market data to verify it.

That’s the pairing Pyth and Exa are testing. Exa handles discovery. Pyth’s MCP tools provide current and historical market data.

Interesting to see how much better research gets when agents can connect the story to the market data behind it.
